subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with nonzero exit codes be nonfatal by default across embedded-agent and isolated cron surfaces?
rationale: Current code has competing semantics: the exec runner preserves nonzero exits as completed output, while shared agent and cron classifiers still promote the same result to error state; choosing the default affects all tool-result consumers.

options.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
options.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in exit policy
options.body: Keep current defaults but add a documented accepted-exit or nonfatal-exit policy surface, accepting extra configuration and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Keep failure semantics and document wrappers
options.body: Document wrapper-based workarounds and close the behavior as intentional, accepting that semantic-exit cron jobs must force exit 0.

recommendation.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
recommendation.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice sits in the shared agent/tool-result boundary where Peter has recent helper/refactor history and the broadest routing signal from available evidence.
